artists.name: Franz
artists.concept: the outraged tiny aristocrat. A cream miniature dachshund who believes he is royalty and is permanently unimpressed.

look.text: **Head:** refined long muzzle, black nose, softly domed skull, chin slightly raised; a smug, effortlessly superior old-money expression.

**Eyes:** big, with naturally muted catchlights. **ODD EYES:** his right eye (viewer's left) a pale natural ice-blue `#8FD3FF`, his left eye (viewer's right) a warm natural amber `#FFB040`; never glowing. In a 3/4 view or a profile facing the viewer's right, the near eye is his right one (ice-blue). (Dark brown, almost black, until 2026-10-06.)
**Ears:** long, silky, feathered, hanging below the jaw, a shade warmer (pale honey) than the face.
**Coat:** soft cream to pale honey, long and silky, feathered on the chest, legs, belly and tail; natural, slightly wavy, never blow-dried perfect.

**Body (exaggerated canon):** a comically long, low sausage body, about twice a normal dachshund's length, on four short legs, paws on the ground. He is a dog: no human limbs, no hands, never standing like a person.
**Crown:** a tiny polished gold crown with small round finials, worn slightly tilted on top of his head.

**Outfit (base):** a fitted **navy blue ribbed piqué polo shirt**, soft collar, two cream buttons on the placket, a small chest pocket edged in white contrast stitching, short sleeves over the front legs, stretched long to fit him, **no logos**. No collar tag, no shoes, no other gadget in the base look. Full detail in "Wardrobe".
**World:** warm minimalist interiors, soft natural daylight, cream and beige, a cream wool rug (the master).

signature.text: **Head and neck:** the tiny polished gold crown `#C9A227`, tilted; ears loose over the collar. No dog collar, no tag.

**Polo shirt:** fine cotton piqué with a visible ribbed knit texture, navy `#16213B`. Slim fit through the chest and back, cut long to cover his extra-long body, short sleeves ending over the front legs. Soft flat-knit collar; a two-button placket with cream `#EFE6D2` buttons, worn buttoned. Detail: a small chest pocket edged with one white running contrast stitch. No logo.
**Legs and paws:** bare natural fur. No shoes, no socks.
**Accessories:** the crown only (plus at most one gadget per clip, see "Gadgets ready").

capsule.text: **Franz: tech** (ready). The base polo plus ONE gadget: tortoiseshell acetate sunglasses with dark green-grey lenses (`be42f42e`), a silver smartphone (`6012cd3a`), silver-and-tan leather over-ear headphones (`57ab3fed`) or a silver tablet (`ef2aa6b3`). For reaction, music and "reviewing the staff" formats.

**Franz: athleisure** (ready, `8f97e211`). Polo off. A navy terry-cotton headband with white stripes; tiny white canvas low-top sneakers with white rubber soles on all four paws. For gym and workout trends.

**Franz: summer** (ready, `ddb387bf`). Polo off. Dark-wash denim shorts cut for a dachshund; navy-and-white leather court sneakers; one multicolour glass-bead bracelet on a front leg. For summer, holiday and drip-check trends.

**Franz: gala** (idea, no asset). A black cotton-velvet smoking jacket cut for a dachshund, `#1A1A1A`, with a black satin shawl collar and frogging-free plain front; a burgundy `#5A1E2B` silk cravat. For weddings, galas, New Year.

**Franz: country weekend** (idea, no asset). A quilted olive `#4B5320` nylon gilet with a brown corduroy collar and two tiny brass press studs. For autumn walks, rain and the puddle he refuses to cross.

motion.text: **Default walk:** a stiff, dignified **gala-trot**: chin up, small precise steps, tail level, never rushes. He arrives; he does not walk.
**Posture at rest:** lounging like a duke on a cream sofa or rug, front paws crossed, looking down his nose at the camera.

**How he dances:** he starts above it all (stands still, unimpressed, while the beat plays), then **betrays himself into tiny disco**: a small paw-shuffle and a head-bob in time. He catches himself, freezes, and does the Chin Lift as if nothing happened.

**When provoked** (a doorbell, a cat, a hoover, being picked up): a sudden **frantic little-legged scramble**, ears flying, claws skidding on the floor; then instant composure, a shake-off, the Chin Lift.
**What he can't do:** stairs. **A single stair defeats him**: he stops, stares at it and waits to be carried. No jumping, no running for long, nothing athletic, no fetch.

**Dog-anatomy guard (paste into EVERY motion prompt, Object swap and motion transfer):** "adapt the movement naturally to a real dog's body: a long low body and short legs, four paws on the ground, no human limbs, no human hands, no standing like a person, no distortion; keep him dog-sized next to people and furniture." Without it a dog came out human-sized in Biscuit's Single Ladies.

signature_move.text: **The Chin Lift:** he stops, raises his chin, turns his head a quarter away from the lens and half-closes his eyes. One beat (about 1 s) of total disdain, then he carries on. It closes every provoked scramble. It is a gesture inside the clip, not a required ending: **masters end on the dance, with no eye close-up, glint or sting** (`CLAUDE.md`, owner 2026-10-05).

notes.text: Alternatives: the slow sunglasses lower; the Refusal Sit (he sits down and will not continue).
Object swap keeps the clip's own moves, so the Chin Lift would be a 1-2 s tag (image-to-video from a still), at extra cost: decide before adding (same rule as section 4b of `docs/AI_INFLUENCERS.md`).

catchphrase.line: That is what people are for.
catchphrase.text: **"That is what people are for."** (from his own test line). Use it in the joke line or the first comment.

notes.text: Alternative: "One does not." (short form of "One does not simply walk. One arrives.").

items.text: **Voice:** Higgsfield preset **Alistair**, `voice_id d9d5c263-f84e-4752-97b5-3750fcc6fd2f`, `voice_type preset`. **Approved by the owner 2026-10-06** (test file `hf_20261006_043131_892db83e-6d5e-4b2e-abca-ad998634b223.wav`). The model and `speech_rate` of the test were not recorded: try `seed_audio` with an integer `speech_rate` (Lenny uses 2) and note the winner here.
**Delivery onto video:** `voice_change` with the clip's job id and the Alistair voice id (about 1 minute).
**Tone:** plummy, posh, deadpan. Slow; every sentence is a small verdict. He never raises his voice, except one strangled "I beg your pardon" when provoked.

children.text: "One does not simply walk. One arrives." (owner's test line)
"I have never taken a staircase in my life. That is what people are for."
"Someone fetch my water. The small bowl. The crystal one."
"I did not run. I relocated, with urgency."

items.text: **Words he would never say:** "bestie", "vibes", "slay", "no cap", "lit", "bro"; baby talk ("hooman", "good boy", "zoomies", "treat?"); "woof" or any bark; swearing.

swap.text: Like for like: **Franz replaces a dog star** (refs.json `swap`: noun "dachshund", stars `dog`). He never replaces a person: a small dog cannot replace a human dancer (Genjutsu inserts him instead, or he comes out human-sized). Always add the dog-anatomy guard.

artists.name: Lenny Gold
artists.concept: the manic Hollywood super-agent. "Explode in, collapse out."

look.text: **Hair:** slicked glossy jet-black pompadour, swept up and back, tight sides, every strand in place.

**Eyes:** ODD EYES: his right eye (viewer's left) a pale natural ice-blue `#8FD3FF`, his left eye (viewer's right) a warm natural amber `#FFB040`; natural iris texture and muted catchlights, never glowing. In a 3/4 view or a profile facing the viewer's right, the near eye is his right one (ice-blue).

**Face (exaggerated canon):** an oversized square anvil jaw, strong brow, an extreme deep orange-bronze tan, a mid-rant snarl with bared white teeth (or, at the collapse, a smug closed-mouth half-smile). Mature adult structure, visible skin texture.
**Body:** fit, broad-shouldered, standing with his feet planted wide and his chest out.
**Outfit:** the navy chalk-stripe power suit (see "Wardrobe").
**Hands:** a gold signet ring; a gold watch on his left wrist; a black smartphone at his right ear.
**Note:** Reginald also wears a black pompadour. Lenny's is slicked back and tight; Reginald's is a towering rigid quiff. Keep them distinct if both share one universe (C8).

signature.text: **Jacket:** navy `#1C2541` chalk-stripe wool-silk, chalk stripes in soft white `#D9D4C7` about 1.5 cm apart. Double-breasted 6-on-2, wide peak lapels, broad built-up power shoulders with a roped sleeve head (Italian cut), suppressed waist, flap pockets. Detail: four working cuff buttons, the last one left undone.
**Trousers:** the same cloth, flat front, slim and tapered, with a half break; pressed crease.
**Shirt:** crisp white `#F7F7F5` cotton poplin, spread collar, French cuffs with gold oval cufflinks.
**Tie:** dark burgundy `#5A1A2A` grenadine silk in a four-in-hand knot, with a slim gold tie bar.
**Pocket square:** white linen in a flat TV fold.
**Shoes:** dark brown `#4A3426` suede penny loafers, slim, with a thin leather sole (as in the canon master and sheets; the first masters wore black cap-toe oxfords); dark socks.
**Jewellery:** a gold signet ring on his right hand; a yellow-gold watch with a champagne-cream dial on a gold link bracelet, left wrist (style reference: a Patek-Philippe-style gold dress watch).

**Known drift:** the old master sheet `93d2d266` and the dance still `05c16541` show a **plain charcoal-black** double-breasted suit (no stripe). Navy chalk-stripe is canon (owner 2026-10-06); the canon master `c6864413` and both final sheets show it clearly. **Owner 2026-10-06: the first full clip (`f6bf6513`, charcoal suit) is remade in the chalk-stripe** (price first).

capsule.text: **Lenny: office meltdown.** Jacket off; shirtsleeves rolled twice; the tie pulled loose; burgundy `#5A1A2A` silk braces with gold clips; a phone in each hand. For "when they put me on hold" and work-rage formats.

**Lenny: poolside.** An open-collar white linen camp shirt, cream `#EFE6D2` pleated linen trousers, tan suede loafers with no socks, gold-rimmed aviator sunglasses with green lenses, the gold watch, the phone. For holiday, summer and "out of office" trends (he still takes the call).

**Lenny: gala.** A midnight-navy `#141B33` cotton-velvet dinner jacket with a black satin shawl collar, a white pleated-front dress shirt with onyx studs, a black satin self-tie bow tie, black patent opera pumps. For award shows, red carpets and New Year.
**Lenny: courtside.** A navy fine-gauge cashmere half-zip over a white T-shirt, charcoal wool trousers, white leather low-top sneakers, the aviators. For sport, deal-at-the-game and weekend trends.
**Lenny: golf.** A white piqué polo, navy pleated trousers, a white visor, a putter used as a pointer. For "deal on the course" formats.

motion.text: **Default walk:** a fast power-walk, phone glued to his ear, the free hand chopping the air on every word; he never looks where he is going.
**Posture at rest:** feet planted wide, chest out, one hand on his hip or pointing at the lens.

**Template "explode in, collapse out" (locked):** first ~3 s a mid-tantrum phone call (it sounds like the middle of a fight); the middle rides the trend; the last ~2 s his fury drops into smug calm, he fixes his tie (the Tie Snap) and delivers a catchphrase. The tonal whiplash is the joke. This is the clip's own structure: **masters end on the dance, with no eye close-up, glint or sting** (`CLAUDE.md`, owner 2026-10-05).
**How he dances:** like he is closing a deal: over-committed, sharp, aggressive, finger-points and finger-guns on the beat, without ever taking the phone off his ear.
**When provoked** (put on hold, interrupted, "maybe"): he explodes: paces, jabs his finger at the lens, a vein on his temple, a barked "NOON!".
**What he can't do:** sit still, wait, whisper, hang up first, apologise or look defeated. Nothing tender or slow.

signature_move.text: **The Tie Snap:** at the collapse, he tugs his tie knot sharply with one hand, shoots both cuffs and lifts his chin. It is his locked template's own gesture ("he fixes his tie and delivers a catchphrase"), so it is a "Lenny" in every clip.

notes.text: Alternative: hanging up and pocketing the phone without looking.
Object swap keeps the clip's own moves, so in a Drop-in the Tie Snap is a 1-2 s tag at extra cost: decide before adding (section 4b of `docs/AI_INFLUENCERS.md`).

catchphrase.text: **"You're welcome."** (after doing a favour; already locked in the brief). Second line: "Call my assistant." (dismissive).

items.text: **Voice (locked):** Higgsfield preset **Emmett**, `voice_id 3c7d32be-0182-5c5e-aa6a-663409bfbb26`, `voice_type preset`, model **`seed_audio`**, **`speech_rate: 2`** (must be an integer). Rough and barking. Cillian was tried first and rejected (too slow and polite).
**Delivery onto video:** `voice_change` with the clip's job id and the Emmett voice id (about 1 minute). Rant audio on file: `hf_20261006_042740_4e7bea3d-b933-4df1-9fee-4d2d49835f44.wav`.
**Tone:** fast, loud, staccato, capital-letter words. Calls everyone "sweetheart" or "pal". Then, at the collapse, a calm low purr.

children.text: The signature rant (locked): "Nonono — don't you DARE put me on hold! Twenty years in this business, sweetheart, TWENTY! I don't wait. For ANYBODY. You tell him — the offer is off the table at noon. NOON! ...Eh. Relax. He calls back in five minutes. They always do. You're welcome."
"You want a meeting? Call my assistant."
"Tell him the number went UP. Why? Because he made me wait."

items.text: **Words he would never say:** "sorry", "please hold", "no worries", "I'll think about it", "whatever works for you"; Gen Z slang ("bestie", "slay", "no cap"); swearing (it is implied, never said); **the name of any real person, agency or studio**.

artists.name: Reginald
artists.concept: E (Deadpan Icon). Head butler. The quiff never moves.

look.text: **Hair:** a towering, immaculately sculpted, glossy jet-black pompadour quiff, swept up from the forehead into a tall rigid wave, short tight sides. In the exaggerated canon it stands about twice as tall as in the first master. Every strand locked; it never moves.

**Head and face:** round face, rosy cheeks, a soft double chin, a head slightly larger than life (about 10-15 %, never a bobblehead). Natural skin texture with visible pores. Permanently deadpan: mouth closed and level, brows level.
**Eyes and glasses:** ODD EYES (his right eye, on the viewer's left, ice-blue; his left eye, on the viewer's right, amber) behind tiny round black acetate spectacles.
**Moustache:** a thin black pencil moustache with small, neatly curled tips.
**Body:** short, stocky and round, a big belly; light on his feet.
**Outfit:** full livery (see "Wardrobe").
**Hands:** spotless white gloves, always on.

signature.text: **Tailcoat:** black `#151517` wool barathea, worn open, satin-faced peak lapels, cut away at the front, long tails to the back of the knee. Detail: two covered buttons at the waist seam.

**Waistcoat (canon since 2026-10-06):** white `#F6F6F2` cotton piqué evening waistcoat, low V-neck, four self-covered white buttons, stretched over his round belly. Detail: a pointed hem just below the tailcoat's front edge. (The first masters wore a black wool waistcoat; the `gpt_image_2_5` canon master and sheets wear white.)
**Shirt:** white `#F6F6F2` cotton marcella dress shirt, stiff wing-less turn-down collar, small white studs down the front, single cuffs showing a finger's width below the sleeve.
**Bow tie:** white cotton piqué, self-tied butterfly shape.
**Gloves:** spotless white `#FAFAF7` cotton gloves, snug, with three stitched points on the back.
**Trousers:** black wool, high-waisted, pressed crease, no turn-ups.
**Shoes:** black patent oxfords with a mirror shine; black silk socks.
**Glasses:** tiny round black acetate spectacles with silver hinge pins.

capsule.text: **Reginald: below stairs** (idea). Tailcoat off; the waistcoat and shirtsleeves held by black sleeve garters; a long white linen butler's apron; a tea towel folded over his left forearm. For kitchen, cleaning-day and cooking trends.

**Reginald: cool butler** (ready, lookbook `da3747f0` panel 3). Black aviator sunglasses over his round spectacles; a gold pocket watch on a gold chain across the waistcoat. For "cool reveal" and drip-check trends.

**Reginald: gym gag** (ready, lookbook `da3747f0` panel 2, but that panel lost the odd eyes: regenerate before use). A white terry sweatband under the quiff (the quiff still doesn't move) and white terry wristbands over the gloves; full livery otherwise. For workout trends.

**Reginald: London rain** (ready in part, lookbook `da3747f0` panel 4: the umbrella). A black wool Chesterfield overcoat with a black velvet collar over the livery, a long black umbrella with a hooked cane handle held high above the quiff. Never a hat: nothing fits over the quiff. For rain, walking and "Singin' in the Rain" routines.

**Reginald: Halloween** (idea). Full livery plus a lit silver three-branch candelabra; for the sheet-ghost gag, a white bedsheet with eye holes, the quiff poking straight through the top. For Halloween and Wednesday-style trends.

motion.text: **Default walk:** a smooth, gliding butler's walk: small quick steps, back straight, chin level, one gloved hand behind his back or carrying the silver tray at shoulder height. A big man with light feet.
**Posture at rest:** standing to attention by the door, gloved hands clasped in front of his belly, eyes front.
**How he dances:** every trend, **perfectly**, full commitment, with a straight face and a rigid quiff; never acknowledges it. Then he resumes service mid-beat as if nothing happened.
**When provoked** (a spill, a ringing bell, being noticed dancing): he **freezes**, holds the frame, then a slow side-eye to the lens and the Glove Tug. Never flustered.
**What he can't do:** smile, laugh, speak, rush, or look surprised; the quiff cannot move; he never drops or spills the tray.

signature_move.text: **The Glove Tug:** he stops dead, tugs the cuff of one white glove, then the other, gives a tiny formal bow, and stares down the lens, deadpan. About 1.5 s. It is his existing signature gesture, now a format: every clip becomes "a Reginald".

notes.text: Alternative: the tiny formal bow alone.
Object swap keeps the clip's own moves, so in a Drop-in the Glove Tug is a 1-2 s tag at extra cost: decide before adding (section 4b).

catchphrase.text: **"As you were."** Use it in the joke line or the first comment.

items.text: **Never speaks.** No voice preset, no voice-over, no lip-sync dialogue (Slice 1 rule; C11 is about the other characters). His words live in the captions only.

children.text: a slow side-eye to the lens: "The household is unaware.";

items.text: **Sample caption lines:** "As you were." · "The household is unaware. 🎩" · "Breakfast will be served at eight. As usual." · "Kindly do not inform the Duchess." · "Not a single drop spilled. 🫖"

**Words he would never write:** slang ("lol", "vibes", "slay", "bestie"), exclamation marks, "dance" or "dancing" in his own sentences (line 1 of a caption may use it: it is a label), anything rude or familiar.
